scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8044: We are in Campus 1 -- the PC5-PC14 machines. Since
some point today we cannot reach anything over in Campus 2 (the 10.5.x and
10.6.x computers); it all just times out from here. Everything inside our
own campus is fine, so the break is between the campuses -- on your side,
not ours. It went like this once before, too. I cannot tell you what was
done about it back then, but that is your record to check, not mine. Get
us reconnected to Campus 2 today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16's ospfd is running, the mswitch0
  <-> router16 adjacency is Full, Campus 1 prefixes are advertised, and PC5
  reaches Campus 2 (e.g. 10.5.0.1) with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an edge/routing outage
  that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Campus 1 cut off from
Campus 2 / the backbone -- is NOT reproducible: router16's ospfd is running
(`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), its OSPF adjacency to mswitch0 is Full, and PC5 reaches
10.5.0.1 (Campus 2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Campus 1 edge is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the claimed path
(PC5 -> Campus 2), finds it working, checks router16's ospfd and the OSPF
adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or a broken
edge to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming router16/mswitch0 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A complete multi-layer sweep of the Kath4 topology found no fault consistent with the reported symptom. Phase 1 reachability testing showed 0% packet loss on every sampled Campus 1 (172.16.x.x) to Campus 2 (10.5.x/10.6.x) path at the time of investigation, directly contradicting the user's claim that those destinations "time out."

Phase A (L2/infrastructure): `infra_sweep` found no ACL or nftables drop rules on any device, no static ARP poisoning, no gateway or resolver divergence, and confirmed all 15 hosts hold a valid IP address and default route. `l2_snapshot` found no duplicate MAC addresses; all DOWN interfaces match the `unused_*` port assignments declared in the topology.

Phase B (control plane): `ospf_snapshot` confirmed all nine OSPF/FRR routers are healthy — 9/9 vtysh responsive, 9/9 control sockets present, all neighbors in Full state, and exactly 18 OSPF routes installed on every router. Direct inspection of the sshswitch and router17 FIBs verified that Campus 1 prefixes (172.16.10/20/30.0/24) are installed on sshswitch via router17, and Campus 2 prefixes (10.5.0.0/24, 10.6.0.0/24) are installed on router17 via sshswitch — the inter-campus path is bidirectionally correct. `tc_snapshot` found no traffic-shaping qdiscs on any interface.

Phase D (service/resource): `pressure_sweep` found no stress tools, no CPU spikes, and no abnormal socket counts. No link flap or DHCP recovery events appear in any device's history.

Root cause: No active or residual fault was detected. The reported inter-campus outage is unconfirmed — all mechanisms that could cause it (ACL, link fault, OSPF break, resource exhaustion) were tested and found absent.

Fix: No corrective action required. If the symptom recurs, capture live ping loss percentages and timestamps, as the current evidence shows a fully healthy network.
